situation (example wording): "How many theft victims in Ohio in 2024?" and "How many thefts in Ohio in 2024?"
what the app does today: NIBRS answers "thefts" by offense, and declines "theft victims" when no table counts that crime by victim. Current Trends declines any "victims" question.
proposed behavior: Property crimes are always counted by offense. When the user asks for victims of a property crime, answer with offenses and state plainly that property crimes are counted by offense, not by victim. Crimes against persons are counted by victim. Exception (Jeff 2026-11-22): when a victim age is named ("juvenile robbery victims", "robbery victims under 18"), the victims of that age are counted for a property crime too (P120); a bare "robberies" or "robbery victims" with no age stays offenses, with the sentence above.
exact default or choices offered: "Theft victims" -> theft offenses, with the sentence "Property crimes are counted by offense, not by victim."
why: One counting unit per kind of crime, as the FBI counts them, stated plainly when the question asked for another.
status: Decided 2026-10-28 (Jeff: give offenses and state plainly that property crimes are not counted by victim); an exception when a victim age is named (Jeff 2026-11-22, audit B9: "Victims when age is named")
test cases: Tests that cite this row: scripts/test-nibrs-plan-language.ts, scripts/test-nibrs-shadow.ts.
